data.ruling: The refutation stands. The figure says no data sheet it read gives an Rp-change-to-output delay, and it cites the FUSB303B's tPDDebounce of 10 to 20 ms in that place. The same FUSB303B data sheet (onsemi FUSB303B/D, September 2024, Rev. 3), Table 8, gives tRpValueChange: minimum 10 ms, maximum 20 ms, "Time a Sink port shall wait before it can determine there has been a change in Rp". The part reports that change as BC_LVL[1:0] in Status register 11h (01 = default current, 10 = 1.5 A, 11 = 3 A). A change sets I_BC_LVL in Interrupt register 14h, which asserts INT_N unless M_BC_LVL masks it. So for the FUSB303B, one data sheet the figure read does give a 10 to 20 ms Rp-change detection time, and that time ends at a register and an interrupt pin. The tPDDebounce the figure cites is the detach time ("Time a Sink port shall wait before it can determine it is detached", 10/15/20 ms), not an Rp-change time. The ruling needs only this contradiction. The TUSB321AI (168 ms) and TUSB321 (133 ms) power-on debounce values and tSinkAdj of 60 ms were not re-read for it. Not stated in Table 8: the delay from the INT_N edge through the firmware's I2C (Inter-Integrated Circuit) read to the charger's input-limit change, and the BQ25713 ILIM_HIZ response time. P5 or a bench measurement still has to supply those. Scope is function, because this is a reported figure for R7's USB-C input-limit behaviour, not a property of any part's lifecycle or identity.

"tPDDebounce | Time a Sink port shall wait before it can determine it is detached | 10 | 15 | 20 | ms". Register map: Status 11h holds BC_LVL[1:0] (thresholds that allow detection of current advertisement on CC: 01 default, 10 1.5 A, 11 3 A). Interrupt 14h bit 2 I_BC_LVL: "Interrupt flagged when a change in BC_LVL[1:0] advertised". Mask bit M_BC_LVL: "Mask the I_BC_LVL interrupt bit from asserting INT_N pin".
